notes:
Topline: Major regional bank. Strong interest in Redwood Dedicated + Private control plane for regulated workloads. Primary negotiation is SLA contract language. Key obs/asks: uptime target, credit schedule, maintenance windows, support RTT, reserved GPU plan.

SLA specifics proposed by Hamilton: 1) Uptime target: they want 99.95% monthly, prefer 99.99% for customer-facing endpoints but willing to accept 99.95% if credit schedule is meaningful. 2) Credits: requested tiered, e.g. <99.99 = 5% credit, <99.95 = 15% credit, <99.5 = 40% of monthly committed fees. Redwood initial counter: 99.95 target with credits starting at 99.9.

Maintenance windows: Hamilton requires maintenance to be limited to a single 2-hour window per month during 02:00-06:00 local; wants automatic 72-hour notice for planned maintenance, 24-hour notice for non-critical updates. They want an explicit policy for emergency security patches (need post-event RCA and reduced credit if no notice).

Support response times asked: P1 (production outage impacting >10% of users) — initial ask: 15 min phone/Slack ack, 1 hour workaround target; P2 — 2 hour ack, 8 hour fix/mitigation; P3 — 24-48 hour. Redwood proposes P1 30 min ack, 4 hour mitigation SLA for Dedicated enterprise. Hamilton pushing for faster.

Reserved GPU planning: Hamilton wants committed pool sizing mapped to committed ARR. Current ask: initial reserved pool 8 x H100-equivalent (to meet 250 concurrent sessions with p95 latency target), with plan to scale to 24 nodes within 12 months. They want guaranteed burst capacity (up to 2x reserved) with pre-negotiated pricing and failover routing to a secondary region.

Throughput/latency guarantees: Their product SLA to customers promises 95th percentile response under 500ms for single-turn responses. They need Redwood SLOs to align so that any service impact doesn't cascade to their SLAs. Hamilton requests p95 < 400ms and p99 < 900ms for established routing. Also wants per-route telemetry and token-level cost allocation for chargebacks across business units.

Other legal/compliance asks: data residency (EU vs NA segmentation), right to audit, retention controls, encryption-at-rest and in-transit with customer-managed KMS, e-discovery support.

Quotes/pullouts: "We can't accept large blind windows for maintenance — it breaks our customer SLAs." — Head of Ops.

Current sentiment: engaged but tough on SLA economics. Legal is careful on credit cap and carveouts for force majeure. Procurement wants a clear uptime-to-credit mapping and a deterministic maintenance policy.
sla_requirements: Hamilton requested SLA parameters for negotiation: uptime target 99.95% preferred 99.99% for prod endpoints; credit schedule tiered (example: 99.99-100: 0%, 99.95-99.99: 5-10%, 99.5-99.95: 25%, <99.5: 50%); maintenance limited to 1x2h monthly window, 72h notice; emergency patch process with RCA within 7 days; support RRT: P1 < 15-30m ack, mitigation 1-4h, P2 ack <2h; telemetry & per-route SLIs exposed via Console
commercial_terms_discussed: Committed ARR tied to reserved GPU capacity; proposed reservation pricing tiers: 8 nodes -> $X/month, 16 nodes -> $Y/month; burst capacity up to 2x with pay-for-burst; billing: monthly with true-up; requested break clauses at 12/24 months if performance targets not met
open_questions_for_engineering: 1) Can runtime guarantee p95/p99 latency at target concurrency with current kernel/quantization profiles? 2) What is realistic burst capacity and warmup time for cold KV caches? 3) Impact of customer-managed KMS on failover and warm standby? 4) Can we expose uptime and maintenance schedule programmatically for their incident system?
procurement_notes: Procurement requests: explicit uptime->credit table, max aggregate credit cap (they want no cap or a cap at 100% of monthly committed fee), indemnity clause review, yearly price escalator cap, SLAs tied to dedicated pool, SLO measurement method (console metrics vs third-party monitoring)
deal_risks: High: SLA economics vs engineering feasibility; legal on data residency and audit access; support staffing for aggressive P1 RRT; potential pricing discount pressure due to competitors (Anthropic/AI cloud)
